liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (3 reviews): The rendition is considered good, though not a major highlight for that specific year; Pigpen's vocal performance is described as vital and strong despite the initial microphone issues [6][9][12]
- **St. Stephen** (3 reviews): The guitar noodles in this jam are described as unique and unlike any other version; The band transitioned directly from the 'One man gathers' verse into Not Fade Away [7][8][9]
- **Dancin' In The Streets** (2 reviews): The performance is enjoyable but does not stand out significantly within the 1970 era; This version is cited as one of the most spontaneous and dynamic performances ever recorded [6][11]
- **Morning Dew** (2 reviews): The rendition is ranked as one of the best versions the listener has ever heard; This performance is identified as one of the best the listener has encountered [13][16]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-05-06.sbd.gans-hall.95.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 14 songs; 88 min; rated 4.13/5 by 15 [1]
- **gd70-05-06.sbd.gans.94.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 88 min; rated 4.51/5 by 49 [3]. Said about its sound: The audio is shaky, with choppy Wier and raw Garcia, though the format is now crisp; The recording quality is noted as excellent, contrasting with many other shows from that year; The tape exhibits good saturation, though the listener prefers later disco-style versions of Dancin' [7][12][15]
- **gd1970-05-06.sbd.gmb.95816.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 88 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: The first minute of the track is 2.5 decibels lower than the remainder due to a reel change [4]
- **gd1970-05-06.156178.msr.zootype.flac16**: source not stated; 14 songs; 88 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]

## Around the show

- Ron McKernan announced a microphone malfunction before the song, noting it did not work well [8]
- The outdoor concert took place in cold weather, though the performance quality remained high [11]
- The song carries extra weight following the Kent State shootings two days prior [17]
- The free outdoor concert was part of a rally protesting the student killings [17]
- The free concert occurred during nationwide campus strikes protesting the Kent State killings [2]
- The show is considered more psychedelic and impactful than other 1970 tapes, including the February 13th date [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-05-06.sbd.gans-hall.95.shnf**: transferred by David Gans and Mike Hall; source: MSR (MIT Reels) 1/2 Track Mono -> Otari MX 55 2 track (playback) -> TC 2000 Studio Effects Processor (using only the A->D converter, no effects) ->Sonic… [1]
- **gd70-05-06.sbd.gans.94.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Eli Polonsky, Rango Keshavan and Darrin Sacks; source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Transferred from MIT WMBR 10-inch mono reels via Otari MX 55 and TC 2000 converter; The transfer chain includes a reel splice at the China Cat Sunflower to I Know You Rider transition [3]
- **gd1970-05-06.sbd.gmb.95816.flac16**: transferred by Bill Koucky; source: Master Soundboard Reels 10", 2-sided, 1/2 Track Mono > DAT x 1 [4]. Also: Reels were transferred to DAT in 1994 by Eli Polansky from WMBR archives for Jim Birkhead [4]
- **gd1970-05-06.156178.msr.zootype.flac16**: transferred by Zootype; source: MSR (MIT Reels) > Sonic Solutions Digital Editing (gans) > DATs > CDRs > EAC > SHN [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by rahvaraamat.ee: [Grateful Dead - Kresge Plaza, M.I.T. Cambridge, M.A., May 6, 1970 WMBR (2024) CD - Rahva Raamat](https://rahvaraamat.ee/et/muusika/muusika/poprock/grateful-dead-kresge-plaza-mit-cambridge-ma-may-6-1970-wmbr-2024/2493090) [19]
